I took quite a long break with many, many NetGalley books to review, but I’m back reading the V&A Fashion Perspectives series. I have enjoyed getting a “behind the scenes” look at these designers, as all save for Quant are no longer with us.

### [**_Dior by Dior_**](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/38748247-dior-by-dior) **, Christian Dior**

> Christian Dior (1905–1957) rocketed to fame with his first collection in 1947 when the “New Look” took the world by storm. This charming and modest autobiography gives a fascinating and detailed insight into the workings of a great fashion house, while revealing the private man behind the high-profile establishment. It is also a unique portrait of classic Paris haute couture of the 1950s and offers a rare glimpse behind the scenes. Dior details his childhood in Granville, the family and friends closest to him, his most difficult years and sudden success, as well as his sources of inspiration and creative processes.

Christian Dior's Dior by Dior

### **Why You Should Read** **_Dior by Dior…_**

I find that these books are all over the place- an autobiography is largely up to the person writing it. And I don’t know if they were asked to write these specifically for the V&A or if they were purchased after for it. In any case, this is one of my favourite autobiographies, period.
